summary: Lens-diverse task review of one diff, each finding adversarially verified by a skeptic panel
logs: 1 minor finding(s) verified by a single skeptic only (important ones got 3).

prior_findings.note:
Closed. _APP_ROLE_SQL (connection_manager.py:110-137) now has a login CTE that holds both session_user and current_user, runs every test for both roles, refuses when session_user <> current_user, and checks ownership with pg_has_role(l.oid, c.relowner, 'MEMBER'). I tested the repo's own verify_app_role against a throwaway local PostgreSQL 16.9 cluster (not a container; since removed):
- A superuser login with ALTER ROLE ... SET role = 'solace_app' is refused. The message names the problem and both roles, e.g. (session_user 'su_role', current_user 'solace_app'), and gives no password or DSN.
- Each of these is refused with only 'owns tables in schema public': a member of a table owner granted WITH INHERIT FALSE; a chained grant member -> mid -(INHERIT FALSE, SET TRUE)-> owner; and INHERIT FALSE, SET FALSE (this one fails closed, which is acceptable).
- A chain through an INHERIT FALSE middle role to the BYPASSRLS solace_migrator is refused as a member of a privileged role.
- Plain solace_app is accepted.

Attempts to defeat the fix all failed:
- ALTER ROLE <su> SET session_authorization = 'solace_app', and the same set IN DATABASE, are accepted by Postgres but have no effect at login. session_user stays the authenticated role, because the login sets session_authorization with override priority. A 'session user differs from the authenticated user' bypass therefore cannot be set up at connection time.
- SECURITY DEFINER does not apply: the check is a top-level statement.
- The role-name comparisons are name = name, which is exact and case-sensitive, so no quoting is involved. The message uses repr.
- The 'no login role row' path works: the outer SELECT has no FROM, so it always returns one row, and roles_found = 0 refuses.
- All pool connections share one DSN, user and database, so per-role, per-database and per-(role, database) defaults are identical for every connection. They can differ only if an operator changes something after the check (TOCTOU), which is outside this fix.

The new unit tests fail against faa52bb's connection_manager.py and postgres.py, shadowed from the base tree blobs: 10 failed, 142 passed. They pass on head: 152 passed.

Closed. The DatabaseConfigError docstring (postgres.py:42-53) now separates the two cases. Settings errors (TLS, a strict host or password, missing or invalid POSTGRES_*) are raised before any connection. The verify_app_role refusal is raised after one connection, and the pool it opened has been closed. The docstring names POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_USER and POSTGRES_SSL_*, and says the role refusal also carries the role names. This matches every raise site: postgres.py:97 (_config_error), connection_manager.py:166 (verify_app_role) and :214 (_validated_settings). The PostgresClient.connect docstring (postgres.py:383-388) now lists every role reason, including membership and the login switch. test_ws026_database_config_error_documents_every_way_it_is_raised fails on faa52bb and passes on head.

findings.problem: The privileged-membership test flags only roles with rolsuper or rolbypassrls (`WHERE p.oid <> l.oid AND (p.rolsuper OR p.rolbypassrls)`). A strict login that is a member of the superuser-equivalent predefined roles pg_execute_server_program, pg_read_server_files or pg_write_server_files therefore passes verify_app_role, even though it can get past FORCE RLS. The repo's own migrate gate already treats these three roles as disqualifying for solace_app; the runtime pool check does not. This gap existed in round 0 and is not a regression from fix1. It is the same precondition class as WS026-SEC-1 (an unusual operator grant plus SQL execution), hence minor.
findings.failure_scenario:
1. ENVIRONMENT=production, and POSTGRES_USER is NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS but an operator has run GRANT pg_execute_server_program TO it. Alternatively, POSTGRES_USER is some login other than solace_app; migrate.py only inspects the named platform roles.
2. get_pool and PostgresClient.connect accept the pool.
3. Any injected SQL runs COPY ... FROM PROGRAM as the database OS user. That user can read the data directory, or run psql as the superuser over the local socket, which uses trust auth on the stock postgres image. Either way it sees every row and can make itself superuser.

Reproduced on a throwaway PG 16.9 cluster with the repo's verify_app_role:
- Role app_prog (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, member of pg_execute_server_program): verify_app_role(environment='production') -> ACCEPTED.
- SELECT count(*) FROM public.t, a FORCE RLS table, returned 0.
- COPY out_rows FROM PROGRAM '<psql> ... -c "SELECT count(*) FROM public.t"' returned 5.
- A pg_read_server_files member was also ACCEPTED. I did not exploit it, because pg_read_binary_file needs its own EXECUTE grant.
findings.fix: Also refuse membership in the three predefined roles. Reuse scripts/db/migrate.py's SUPERUSER_EQUIVALENT_ROLES, for example `AND (p.rolsuper OR p.rolbypassrls OR p.rolname IN ('pg_execute_server_program', 'pg_read_server_files', 'pg_write_server_files'))`, or add a separate reason such as 'is a member of a superuser-equivalent role'. pg_has_role(l.oid, p.oid, 'MEMBER') already covers chained and non-inheriting grants. Add a real-PG test that grants pg_execute_server_program to a throwaway login and expects DatabaseConfigError. Optionally also match migrate.py's NOREPLICATION pin for the app role.
findings.evidence:
- connection_manager.py:130-136: the member_of_privileged_role EXISTS filters on `(p.rolsuper OR p.rolbypassrls)` only, and nothing else in _APP_ROLE_SQL looks at predefined roles.
- scripts/db/migrate.py:107-109 defines SUPERUSER_EQUIVALENT_ROLES = (pg_execute_server_program, pg_read_server_files, pg_write_server_files), with the comment 'Predefined roles the PostgreSQL docs call superuser-equivalent'. migrate.py:351-353 refuses a platform role that is a member of any of them. migrate.py:84-87 also pins solace_app NOREPLICATION. I did not test REPLICATION as an RLS bypass and do not claim it is one.
- PostgreSQL docs, Predefined Roles (quoted from memory, not fetched this session; it matches migrate.py's comment): these roles 'bypass all database-level permission checks when accessing files directly and they could be used to gain superuser-level access'.
- The probe output quoted in failure_scenario: ACCEPTED, 0 rows visible under FORCE RLS, 5 rows counted via COPY FROM PROGRAM.
- Infrastructure/init-db never grants these roles, so the gap needs operator action. That is why the severity is minor.

votes.reason: The code matches the finding. The member_of_privileged_role test in connection_manager.py (line 134) is `p.oid <> l.oid AND (p.rolsuper OR p.rolbypassrls)`. A grep of src/solace_infrastructure/database found no reference to pg_execute_server_program, pg_read_server_files or pg_write_server_files. Membership in those roles therefore passes verify_app_role. The repo's own scripts/db/migrate.py defines SUPERUSER_EQUIVALENT_ROLES (line 109) with exactly those three and refuses them for platform roles, so the runtime check is weaker than the migrate gate. I did not re-run the finding's COPY ... FROM PROGRAM reproduction, but it follows from the SQL as written. The severity is minor: the gap needs an unusual operator grant, which init-db never makes, plus SQL execution. It is not a regression from fix1.
